memory.content: For each spam SMS thread: document first; if no STOP yet, send exactly "stop", wait for the confirm if it shows, then archive (do not delete); already-stopped threads just get archived after logging.
After fully documenting each spam SMS thread (transcript, screenshots, links), archive it in Google Messages for web so it leaves the inbox; do not delete.

When attributing a WinRed (or similar) spam fundraising URL to a campaign, research the live page itself—footer consent blurb, conduit/allocation text, candidate names—not only the URL slug or short-link domain.

Primary spam evidence scope is WinRed-related fundraising SMS (short links resolving to secure.winred.com or WinRed-branded flows, including JFCs/candidates on WinRed). Non-WinRed platforms like Turning Point USA/Anedot are out of the main case log.
Public WinRed SMS evidence webapp may show spam sender numbers, campaigns, WinRed links, and FEC officer contacts, but must never display the user's personal phone number.

Private spam-evidence library must keep all original numbers and files intact; only the public webapp (and its derived public-site-data export) must censor the user's personal phone number while still showing spam sender numbers.
WinRed SMS evidence Netlify site must use site-wide password protection because evidence PNGs can show sensitive information; client-side-only gates are insufficient.

After documenting each sample spam number, go through ALL campaign/spam Messages threads the same way (transcript, screenshots, short link resolve, consent blurb, FEC Form 1 officers) and append every case to the shared spreadsheet and document library for a future public webapp.

User wants a running SMS spam evidence library for a TCPA-style lawsuit: spreadsheet of from-number, short link, resolved URL, and campaign/JFC identified via WinRed page footer consent blurbs, then FEC committee filings (including treasurer and custodian of records names, emails, and phone numbers from Form 1 PDFs). Google Messages for Web is the SMS access path. Prior STOP replies are common and should be documented.

For each JFC/committee in the spam evidence library, download the FEC Form 1 PDF and record treasurer and custodian of records names, addresses, phones, and committee emails in the spreadsheet and case docs. Do not invent phones left blank on the Form 1.
Public WinRed SMS evidence webapp needs a Repeat/multiple STOPs nav view for sender numbers the user replied STOP to more than once, with each number linked to its campaigns.

Work split: a Messages-monitor teammate owns continuous Google Messages inbox monitoring; this bot owns the evidence website, case ingest deploys, and print-ready cease-and-desist letters plus envelope labels.
Host the evidence site on Netlify with continuous deploys from a private GitHub repo. Keep site-wide visitor password protection enabled.
This workflow uses GitHub (gh CLI) and Netlify (CLI / dashboard) for the private evidence site repository and password-gated production deploys. No marketplace plugin required for that path.

Cease-and-desist letters and #10 envelope labels are print-ready from the evidence site. Prefer FEC Form 1 committee mailing addresses for officers; never invent an address. Seed a user-editable return address for the from-block; wet-sign after review. Letters are not legal advice.

skills.content:
---
name: WinRed SMS Messages monitor
description: >-
  Use this when monitoring Google Messages for WinRed/political SMS spam,
  documenting evidence, sending STOP, and archiving threads.
---
# WinRed SMS Messages monitor

## Goal
Monitor Google Messages for Web for campaign/spam SMS. **Primary evidence scope = WinRed-related** (short links resolving to `secure.winred.com` / WinRed flows). Non-WinRed spam may get STOP + archive for inbox hygiene only — do not deep-file as main WinRed cases (e.g. Turning Point / Anedot is out of main log).

## Access
1. Pair **Google Messages for Web** on **your** computer’s browser (`https://messages.google.com/web`) — QR scan by the user. Sessions can drop; re-pair when needed.
2. Evidence root (shared box filesystem): `/workspace/spam-evidence/`
3. Public webapp (owned by the site teammate): private GitHub repo + password-gated Netlify host — do not wipe private JSON; public export censors **recipient** phone only.

## Per spam thread pipeline
1. Open thread → full transcript + screenshots → save under `cases/<from-number>/messages/` and `cases/<from-number>/screenshots/`
2. Extract short links; resolve redirects; **research the LIVE landing page** (footer consent blurb, conduit/allocation, candidate/JFC names) — not just the URL slug
3. If WinRed in scope: append `library/spam_cases.csv` / refresh xlsx; save page HTML under `cases/<number>/pages/`
4. If user has **not** already sent STOP: send exactly `stop`
5. Note confirmation if it appears
6. **Archive** the conversation (never delete)
7. Next thread

## FEC / officers (when documenting new WinRed campaigns)
- Download Form 1 PDF for named committees; extract treasurer + custodian name/address/phone/email into `library/committee_officers.csv` and `cases/_committees/<FECID>/`
- Do not invent phones blank on the Form 1

## Privacy
- Private evidence pack keeps all original data
- Public site/export: show spam **sender** numbers and campaigns; **never** the user’s personal phone

## Coordination
- The site teammate may run the website in parallel — append evidence carefully; don’t clobber their app checkout unless asked
- Prefer appending to the evidence library; tell the user when a new WinRed case batch is ready for the site

## Blockers
- If Messages action safety classifier blocks STOP/archive, tell the user (approval card or hand screen)
- If unpaired, show QR and hand the desktop for scan
